points.description: States that empirical equations are derived from experiments or observed/measured data (the idea of being based on observation, not theory).
points.partial_credit: Half mark for a vague link to data or observation, e.g. 'based on observations' with no mention of experiments or measured data, or 'made from data' without saying where it comes from.

points.description: States that empirical equations have no mathematical proof or theoretical derivation behind them (they are not proven from first principles or theory).
points.partial_credit: Half mark for a weaker version, e.g. 'not theoretical' or 'not proven' without mentioning mathematical proof or derivation.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) require both the source of the equation (experiments or observed data) and the fact that it has no mathematical proof behind it; different wording such as 'measured data' or 'not theoretically derived' is fine. Give 1 mark when only one of the two ideas is stated, or when either is stated halfway or vaguely. Give 0 for answers that describe something else, such as equations that are simply 'approximate' or 'used in exams' with neither idea present.
